subject.title: Allow before_agent_start hooks to override prompt

question: Should installed plugins be allowed to replace the user-authored prompt through the shared prompt-build API, and if so what precedence and audit boundary should govern that authority?
rationale: Current code has a mature additive hook seam, but full prompt replacement changes the security and user-intent contract rather than repairing an established broken behavior.

options.title: Approve a scoped shared replacement field
options.body: Add a single `prompt` field to the primary prompt-build result, enforce the existing prompt-injection policy, define deterministic precedence, and require PI/CLI/Codex parity tests.

options.title: Keep hooks additive and blocking only
options.body: Reject user-prompt replacement and direct context-limit mitigation toward blocking, compaction, or owner-controlled preprocessing paths.

options.title: Defer pending an audited transformation design
options.body: Pause the API until maintainers define plugin provenance, user visibility, and logging expectations for rewritten prompts.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped shared replacement field
recommendation.body: Add a single `prompt` field to the primary prompt-build result, enforce the existing prompt-injection policy, define deterministic precedence, and require PI/CLI/Codex parity tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the Codex prompt-build bridge that must remain contract-compatible with the shared hook API.
